assumptions: Routes in this inventory and the current map are proposals, not a verified application routing contract; S08b is a mobile editor pane.
Screen titles use titleEn exactly; S04 retains Welcome / first visit although its master is named Welcome.
The seven journeys follow design-system §9 in order; titleAr uses the corresponding desktop flow name without its numeric prefix.
Map journey assignments are retained as primary ownership; shared screens can participate in other journeys.
The history and save-conflict prototype flows both belong to J4 Return and revise; prototype flow numbers are not journey IDs.

Product states are deduplicated across desktop/mobile by name; use kind="product" and exclude kind="snapshot". The published export9 map has 150 product-state masters for 75 logical states, plus 120 record/fixture snapshots (270 state masters total).

dialogs covers all 23 map dialog/sheet masters as 13 logical names after removing Dialog/Sheet prefixes and deduplicating across platforms; Change password: mismatch remains separate. Component-set dialogs include their default/error/expired or blocked variants; exact parent/platform coverage is in map.dialogs.

popups is the union of logical names from current map.navigation after removing Popup ·, deduplicated within each surface/platform and then across shared names. Preserve named record/fixture variants; exact surface coverage and node IDs remain in navigation. Desktop has 157 popup frames, mobile 127 and Website: Landing 2; these are prototype artifacts, not production routes.

Commercial fixture meanings come from design-system §10; the current map.fixtures supplies the shared synthetic person/contact, dates and transaction reference alongside the same illustrative Start/Focus data.

The current fixtures explicitly include Sara Alotaibi / سارة العتيبي, sara@example.com, +966 50 123 4567, MCV-2026-00128 and renewal/allowance-reset/last-edit dates. They are synthetic; no structured employer/university fixture records are supplied by map.fixtures.
Documentation dates and Figma node references are provenance, not product fixtures.
Prices, quotas, usage, tax arithmetic and upload limits are fixtures, not approved production configuration or policy.
The easing curve is a proposal; the docs specify the 120/200/320 ms durations only.
Mobile masters keep the documented 390 px reference breakpoint instead of the skill default 402 px; this does not mandate a production CSS breakpoint.
Noto Sans Arabic, Noto Sans and Noto Serif await owner approval D11; font binaries are not bundled and document typography is independent.
D04 OWNER DECIDED 2026-11-04: PDF-only launch; Word unavailable. Future A05 targets Microsoft 365 Word Windows/Mac plus Google Docs, single-column templates and default fonts.
Google sign-in remains gated pending data-flow review and a matching S30 re-authentication path.
Moyasar is the selected provider, not a fixture; interface copy stays neutral as a Saudi payment gateway until merchant activation and naming permission.
Merchant fees, enabled methods, recurring eligibility, production offer, tax, entitlements and cancellation/refund policy remain unapproved.
Masters depict a Focus subscriber; the S24 Start plan state is the paid-flow entry and new-user screens use Start allowances.
S35 legal text is a draft pending owner approval; landing copy must reflect enabled features without fabricated claims.
The old email stays active until the new one is confirmed; account changes require real confirmation and persistence.
Deletion requires the approved identity, retention and backup process; no immediate deletion everywhere or invented retention duration is implied.
Switching AR/EN changes the interface only; saved CV content and Arabic/English document versions remain isolated.
States, modal forms and prototype simulators are not separate routes or evidence of working services.
AI processing and integrations remain subject to security approval; unapproved AI routes fail closed.
Employer B2B, public professional profiles, automatic applications and interview services are outside this personal design scope.
Published component libraries, Code Connect bindings and application acceptance gates are not established by this inventory.
This inventory uses the supplied read-only snapshot, without fresh live Figma or application verification.

State masters not listed in screens[].states are record/fixture snapshots (the same UI showing another demo record, step or plan context) kept so the click-through tells one consistent story; the map marks them kind="snapshot". Build the product states; do not create routes or components per snapshot.
Prototype scope was capped on 2026-11-03: remaining multi-step state-memory paths are accepted limits instead of adding more snapshot copies.
The click-through does not demonstrate the English interface or dark mode (EN and moon toggles hidden on prototype instances); see English (LTR) and the Dark showcase.
Mobile sheets/popups are device-size frames; correct bottom anchoring in Play needs the owner to set a Custom device (390 wide mobile, 1440x900 desktop) on each prototype page.
S08b · Editor: preview is a mobile-only pane of the S08 editor (desktop shows the preview beside the editor); route is a proposal.

Publication reconciliation uses export9 structural records, navigation and fixtures dated 2026-11-03. Current assumptions/counts are synchronized with the published map; superseded count and S36 requirement conflicts are resolved. Historical QA records remain unchanged. No live Figma calls were made in this publication lane.

The published map contains 69 component sets plus 2 standalone helper components; inventory.components lists the 69 component-set names. There are 40 screen records (S01-S39 plus mobile-only S08b), 10 English-interface masters, 270 state masters (150 product and 120 snapshots) and 23 dialog/sheet masters. Prototype navigation has 424 desktop, 425 mobile and 4 website frames, including popups.

Mobile OTP masters/states/components are present in the exported design and published map. Their behavior remains proposed and gated under B-C17/B-C18 and A14-A16; the design does not approve a provider, real-number send, live route or release.
S37-S39 use J1 as their primary journey and are reused by J2 and J6; their route labels are design proposals pending TanStack Router reconciliation.
Phone and code values display LTR Latin digits within Arabic RTL UI; Arabic-Indic and Eastern Arabic input is normalized before validation.
Simulator: SMS is prototype-only on both desktop and mobile and never sends an SMS or authorizes authentication.

D20 OWNER DECIDED 2026-11-04: Phase 1 password-bearing mobile signup/login, optional email, signup/settings verification, verified-mobile SMS reset and 8 hashed one-time recovery codes. Preserve enrolled MFA at next sign-in; SMS-only sign-in stays Phase 2 off. New states are specified in specs/otp-spec.md and await publication; A14-A16 remain gates.
rules: Implement from the masters on 'Screens: Desktop' and 'Screens: Mobile' (one master per screen). Prototype pages hold instances plus prototype-only simulators; never implement 'Popup · Simulator…' or 'Popup · Note…' frames.
Arabic RTL is the full set. 'English (LTR)' mirrors key screens only; the English interface uses the same masters' components with Dir=LTR variants and the Type collection in English mode.
State frames (names with ': state') are states of the same route, not new routes or tables.
Dialog and sheet masters on 'States & Patterns' are the content of modal forms; desktop renders the Dialog, mobile the Sheet.
Interface language is not document language: never translate or reorder saved CV content when the interface language changes.
Node IDs are a dated snapshot. Re-read the live node before implementing; if a name no longer matches, refresh this file instead of guessing.

State frames ('Sxx · Title: state') are states of the same route, not new routes.
Node IDs are a dated snapshot: re-read the live node before implementing and regenerate this file if names drift.
